messages.content: What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?

function.name: calculate_maximum_height
function.description: Calculate the maximum height an object will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with an initial velocity, ignoring air resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity in meters per second. This is a float type value.

gravity.description: The acceleration due to gravity in meters per second squared, default value is 9.8. This is a float type value.

The correct answer: acceleration due to gravity is constant ~9.8 m/s^2 downward. So the ball will accelerate at -9.8 m/s^2. But maybe they want to compute maximum height using the function. The function signature: calculate_maximum_height(initial_velocity, gravity?). So we can call it with initial_velocity=5. That returns maximum height. But the question: "What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?" That is ambiguous. I'd interpret as "What is the maximum height?" But they explicitly mention acceleration. So maybe they want to know the acceleration due to gravity. So answer: -9.8 m/s^2. But we can also mention that acceleration is constant regardless of initial velocity. So the ball will accelerate at -9.8 m/s^2 (downwards).
